To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the morphology of mitochondrial cristae is dynamic and that Ca2+ signals regulate the dynamics of cristae membranes in a spatially confined manner.
mitochondrial cristae dynamics are reduced by intracellular Ca2+ and that this effect is independent from the mitochondrial matrix Ca2+.
mitochondrial cristae membranes are highly dynamic organelles that are regulated by Ca2+ signals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of super-resolution microscopy to investigate sub-mitochondria structures and dynamics.
the development of new super-resolution microscopy techniques and their application to the investigation of mitochondrial structure and dynamics.
the dynamics of mitochondrial substructures and its regulation by intracellular Ca2+ signaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ca2+ release from the endoplasmatic reticulum decelerates the dynamics of the cristae membrane in the junction between the mitochondria and the reticulum.
Ca2+ release from the ER reduces the dynamics of CM within the mitochondrial junctions to the ER.
the dynamics of the inner membrane is a key parameter to control mitochondrial function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2+-dependent CM-dynamics is essential for a well balanced functional (Ca2+)-interplay between mitochondria, the endoplasmatic reticulum and the cytoplasm.
the dynamics of CM are controlled by OPA1 and Ca2+, and that Ca2+ release from the ER reduces the mobility of CM in MAMs.
mitochondrial cristae dynamics are spatially and functionally regulated by intracellular calcium signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
super-resolution SIM can be used to study mitochondrial dynamics and substructures in live cells.
super-resolution microscopy can provide new insights into the dynamics of sub-mitochondria structures and the regulation of these structures by intracellular messengers.
super-resolution microscopy can be used to quantify the dynamics and the architecture of the inner mitochondrial membranes, which are essential to understand the function of mitochondria.
